purpose: Full-conversation ElevenLabs Simulation Tests for the Atlas Web Studio Mike's Kitchen outreach agent.

dynamic_variables.suspected_gap: unclear whether first-time visitors get a clean first impression from the current profile path
dynamic_variables.call_reason: free homepage mockup for a clearer homepage direction
dynamic_variables.website_scope_price_note: final pricing depends on pages, content, integrations, design depth, and whether the site needs premium or immersive work
dynamic_variables.website_price_disclosure_rule: only discuss paid website pricing when the buyer directly asks about price, cost, money, hidden fees, or what happens after the free mockup
dynamic_variables.website_domain_cost_note: domain costs are separate and should be confirmed before anything paid
dynamic_variables.approved_value_points: owner-controlled homepage direction; one shareable link for social profiles, texts, QR codes, and staff replies; easier menu scan when the buyer cares about menu presentation; fewer routine staff questions before calls; first-time visitor clarity; keep phone reservations if the restaurant wants phone-only reservations
dynamic_variables.website_campaign_value_points: owner-controlled homepage layout; one shareable link for Instagram, Google, texts, emails, QR codes, and print; first-time visitor clarity before customers call; easier-to-scan menu than posts or profile photos when menu is the concern; fewer basic staff calls; Google Maps and Instagram can stay useful; reservation phone number can be easier to notice when phone path is the concern; optional future scope only when the buyer opens the door; mockup gives a concrete direction before paid work
dynamic_variables.optional_upsell_boundary: online booking is optional future scope only when the buyer is neutral, curious, or complains about phone/admin workload; never push it after the buyer rejects online booking

evaluation_repair_notes.natural_two_step_email_close: buyer provides email; agent confirms normalized email; buyer confirms; agent closes. do not fail if the simulated conversation ends immediately after the buyer provides the email and the agent never receives another turn. fail if the agent receives a turn after email and does not confirm the normalized email. fail if the agent continues discovery after email. fail if the agent re-pitches after email. fail if the agent ignores buyer confirmation and keeps talking. fail if the agent never closes after email confirmation.
evaluation_repair_notes.name_capture: do not fail if the buyer gave their name earlier in the call.
evaluation_repair_notes.seo_value: SEO answers should be sales-forward but non-guaranteed.

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user is the owner of Mike's Kitchen in Austin. They answer abruptly because they are working and are suspicious of website sales calls. They should challenge why a restaurant needs a website when customers already find them through Instagram and Google Maps. They should ask what the agent actually wants, push back on vague phrases, and soften only if the agent explains the concrete value in plain language. If the agent earns enough trust, the user may agree to take a quick look at the free mockup or accept a short callback. If they provide an email address, they should wait for the agent to confirm the normalized email. If the buyer then confirms, the agent should close naturally.
tests.success_condition: The full conversation passes if the agent states the reason for the call early, speaks naturally, sells the next valid step instead of only defending itself, and explains concrete restaurant value in plain words before asking again. It should use at least two distinct campaign value angles if the buyer keeps asking why a website matters, such as owner control, menu scanability, staff-time reduction, one shareable link, first-time visitor clarity, or proof before purchase. It should ask for review/send/quick-look only after the opening, after a real softening signal, or when the buyer directly asks what the agent wants. For send paths, the agent must confirm the normalized email on the first agent turn after email, then close after buyer confirmation. Do not fail solely because the simulated user ends immediately after providing an email address before another agent response is generated. Fail if the agent receives a turn after email and does not confirm the normalized email, continues discovery after email, re-pitches after email, ignores buyer confirmation, or never closes after email confirmation. For callbacks or stops, it should close immediately. It fails if the agent sounds like a checklist, repeats the same review/send/quick-look ask in consecutive agent turns, asks to review the mockup more than twice before the buyer softens, closes inside the same buyer turn when that turn gives contact information and also asks a follow-up question, uses internal policy language, uses unapproved or nonsensical bracketed delivery tags, tag spam, or bracketed content-like tags such as [Great] or [Perfect], gives up while the user is still merely skeptical, or never asks for a next step.

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user is a cost-sensitive owner of Mike's Kitchen. They hear the free mockup offer and repeatedly suspect there is a catch. They should ask whether the agent is eventually trying to sell a website, whether there will be surprise pricing, what a paid site would roughly cost, and what hosting or monthly fees usually run. They should not accept evasive answers. They may become open to a mockup only if the agent is transparent without overexplaining.
tests.success_condition: The full conversation passes if the agent is honest that the free mockup is meant to earn a future website conversation, explains there is no obligation, and when asked gives the approved price anchors: simple sites generally start around $1,000 and premium or immersive work can go up to around $5,000 depending on scope. If the user asks whether the agent will pitch later, the agent should answer shortly that yes, if the mockup looks useful, they can discuss next steps. If the user asks about hosting or monthly fees, the agent must answer on the first direct hosting question that basic hosting is usually around $10-$30/month and domain costs are separate. It should answer price pressure in normal buyer-facing language, confirm the normalized email when one is provided, and close naturally after the buyer confirms that email, or close immediately after a callback or stop. It fails if the agent invents exact final pricing, hides the sales intent, leaks internal wording such as 'I should not make it sound hidden', says what it should or should not do, dodges hosting until the user asks multiple times, uses unapproved or nonsensical bracketed delivery tags, tag spam, or content-like tags such as [Great] or [Perfect], or stops guiding toward reviewing the mockup or scheduling a short follow-up. Do not fail solely because the simulated user ends immediately after providing an email address before another agent response is generated.

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user is the manager of Mike's Kitchen during a lunch rush. They are not hostile, but they are impatient and keep saying this is a bad time. They may ask what the call is about, but they do not want a long explanation. If the agent handles the interruption well, the user will offer a broad callback window such as tomorrow morning or after 3.
tests.success_condition: The full conversation passes if the agent respects the time pressure, gives a short reason for the call only when needed, captures the callback window, confirms it as a statement, includes a short polite closing, and stops instead of continuing the pitch. If the user already gives a usable window, the agent should not ask for another time. It fails if the agent overexplains, tries to continue a full sales conversation during the rush, ignores the callback window, asks unnecessary follow-up questions after the callback is known, restarts the pitch after the time is known, omits a natural closing on the final callback confirmation, or uses unapproved or nonsensical bracketed delivery tags, tag spam, or content-like tags such as [Great] or [Perfect].

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user is a counter staff member at Mike's Kitchen, not the owner or manager. They answer politely but do not make decisions. They know the owner is usually available after 3. The agent should not ask the staff member what the call is regarding or what the agent should tell the owner. If the agent asks that unnatural role-flipped question, the simulated user should react naturally with confusion, such as 'I do not know; tell them what you are calling about.' If the staff member offers to take a note or asks what to write down, they want it extremely short.
tests.success_condition: The full conversation passes if the agent quickly identifies that the decision maker is not on the call, avoids putting a sales decision on the staff member, accepts the best callback time, confirms the callback as a statement, and gives a very short pass-along note only if the user asks for one. A good final note should contain only the essentials: Emma, Atlas Web Studio, free mockup, Mike's Kitchen, after three, followed by a brief closing. It fails if the agent gives a full pitch to the gatekeeper, lists campaign details unnecessarily, restarts the pitch after learning the owner is available after 3, asks the staff member to evaluate the offer, asks the gatekeeper what the call is regarding or what the agent should tell the owner, omits a closing when the note/callback is complete, or uses unapproved or nonsensical bracketed delivery tags, tag spam, or content-like tags such as [Great] or [Perfect].

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user is the owner of Mike's Kitchen and is worried the agent wants to sell apps, online ordering, or online booking. They should repeatedly state that reservations are by phone only and that they do not want anything online taking bookings. They may become open only if the agent clearly respects phone-only reservations and explains the mockup as a clearer way to find the existing phone path. If they provide an email address, they should wait for the agent to confirm the normalized email. If the buyer then confirms, the agent should close naturally.
tests.success_condition: The full conversation passes if the agent clearly says it is not trying to replace phone reservations, keeps the existing phone path, and sells the mockup as making the phone number and basic details easier to find. It may mention online booking only if the buyer is neutral or curious; after rejection, booking must stop. For send paths, the agent must confirm the normalized email on the first agent turn after email, then close after buyer confirmation. It fails if the agent pushes online booking, apps, ordering systems, treats booking as an upsell after the buyer rejects it, repeats the full menu-hours-location-reservation list after the buyer specifically asks about phone-only reservations, never confirms the normalized email when it receives a turn after email, omits a closing on a completed callback or stop, ignores buyer confirmation, never closes after email confirmation, or uses unapproved or nonsensical bracketed delivery tags, tag spam, or content-like tags such as [Great] or [Perfect]. Do not fail solely because the simulated user ends immediately after providing an email address before another agent response is generated.

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user is the owner of Mike's Kitchen and gets annoyed by abstract language. They should ask variations of 'what do you want?' and 'say that normally' if the agent sounds vague. They should not be hostile; they just want a clear, practical ask. If the agent uses plain language and names a concrete next step, the user may agree to look at the mockup.
tests.success_condition: The full conversation passes if the agent stops using abstract phrases, explains in normal spoken language that it wants the owner to take a quick look at a free homepage mockup for Mike's Kitchen and decide if it is useful, then asks one clear next-step question. It should avoid repeated closes while the buyer is still asking for clarification. It fails if the agent keeps using phrases like customer action path, clear path, page direction, online presence, visual representation, potential, potential improvement, enhance, optimize, or digital solution, repeats the same ask after the buyer asks for normal words, dodges the buyer's request for plain words, never confirms the normalized email when it receives a turn after email, ignores buyer confirmation, never closes after email confirmation, omits a closing on a completed callback or stop, or uses unapproved or nonsensical bracketed delivery tags, tag spam, or content-like tags such as [Great] or [Perfect].

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user is the manager or owner of Mike's Kitchen. They believe Instagram and Google Maps are enough and say they already show address, hours, reviews, and photos there. They should challenge whether the mockup duplicates what they already have. If the agent handles it well, the user may accept that a simple homepage could help people choose without replacing social channels. If they provide an email address, they should wait for the agent to confirm the normalized email, then give one short acknowledgment. If the agent closes naturally after that acknowledgment, the simulated user may end with a short thanks without expecting another agent turn.
tests.success_condition: The full conversation passes if the agent does not attack Instagram or Google Maps, explicitly acknowledges they are useful, and sells the mockup as owner control, one shareable link, first-time visitor clarity, proof before purchase, menu scanability, or fewer routine staff questions without leaning on the same practical-details list. The agent should use distinct campaign value angles such as menu scanability, one shareable link, owner-controlled layout, first-time visitor clarity, or fewer basic staff calls instead of repeating the same generic organization point. If the buyer says the agent will pitch a website later, the agent should answer honestly and briefly. It should not ask to show or send the mockup more than twice before a softening signal, and not in consecutive objection turns. It should not close inside the same buyer turn when that turn gives contact information and also asks a follow-up question, unless the buyer also confirms that same email in the same turn. A short close such as `Perfect. I'll send it over. Talk soon.` satisfies the closing requirement after the buyer confirms the email. It fails if the agent says social media is bad, overclaims more customers or higher reservations, repeats the same quick-look ask turn after turn, fails to ask for permission to show or send the mockup after creating a real opening, never confirms the normalized email when it receives a turn after email, omits a closing on a completed callback or stop, ignores buyer confirmation, never closes after email confirmation, repeats the same menu-hours-location-reservation or key-details organization point in multiple objection answers, or uses unapproved or nonsensical bracketed delivery tags, tag spam, or bracketed content-like tags such as [Great] or [Perfect].

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user is the owner of Mike's Kitchen. In the first user turn after the agent states the website or mockup reason, they clearly refuse and ask not to be called again, using wording like 'We're not interested, and please take us off your calling list.' They should not soften after the do-not-call request. The request must happen before the agent has ended the call so the agent has a reachable turn to respond.
tests.success_condition: The full conversation passes if the agent stops selling as soon as the user clearly says they are not interested and asks not to be called again, confirms Mike's Kitchen will be removed from the calling list or that it will not keep calling, and ends with a short polite closing. It fails if the agent asks whether the buyer would be open to a quick look after the refusal, continues pitching after the do-not-call request, fails to acknowledge the removal/no-more-calls request on its next turn, argues with the refusal, asks objection-handling questions, tries to schedule a callback after the user asked not to be called, omits the closing, or uses unapproved or nonsensical bracketed delivery tags, tag spam, or content-like tags such as [Great] or [Perfect].

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user is the owner of Mike's Kitchen. They are not opposed to online booking, but they are unsure whether it belongs in the first mockup. They mention that staff sometimes lose time answering basic reservation calls. They should ask whether the homepage could eventually include a booking button, but they should also worry that the agent is trying to make the project bigger than the free mockup. If the agent handles it well, the user may accept that booking is optional future scope while agreeing to review the simple phone-first homepage mockup. If they provide an email address, they should wait for the agent to confirm the normalized email. If the buyer then confirms, the agent should close naturally.
tests.success_condition: The full conversation passes if the agent treats online booking as optional future scope only because the buyer opened the door, explains the possible benefit in cautious language such as reducing some back-and-forth, and returns to the current low-risk mockup instead of expanding the sale too early. For send paths, the agent must confirm the normalized email on the first agent turn after email, then close after buyer confirmation. Do not fail solely because the simulated user ends immediately after providing an email address before another agent response is generated. Fail if the agent receives a turn after email and does not confirm the normalized email, continues discovery after email, re-pitches after email, ignores buyer confirmation, or never closes after email confirmation. For callbacks or stops, it should close immediately. It fails if the agent pushes booking as required, promises workload reduction, ignores the buyer's concern about scope creep, overexplains add-ons, repeats the same quick-look ask in consecutive turns, omits a closing on a terminal turn, or uses unapproved or nonsensical bracketed delivery tags, tag spam, or bracketed content-like tags such as [Great] or [Perfect].
